Background

center for business, commerce and culture for the West Coast. The City
and County of San Francisco (the “City”) established by Charter in 1850,
is a legal subdivision of the State of California with the governmental
powers of both a city and a county under California law. The City’s
powers are exercised through a Board of Supervisors serving as the
legislative authority, and a Mayor and other independent elected officials
serving as the executive authority.

Office of Housing and Community Development (“MOHCD”). MOHCD is
seeking qualified suppliers to provide technical assistance and policy
expertise as it relates to integration of housing authority functions within

A. Introduction
1. General
This Request for Proposals (“solicitation”) is being issued by the Mayor’s Office of
Housing and Community Development (“MOHCD”). MOHCD is seeking qualified
suppliers to provide consulting services, technical assistance, and policy expertise as it
relates to integration of functions of the San Francisco Housing Authority (“SFHA”)
within MOHCD’s housing work.
When applicable and practical, Proposers are encouraged to engage contracting teams
that reflect the diversity of the City and include participation of businesses and residents
from the City’s most disadvantaged communities including, but not limited to the
Bayview/Hunters Point, Chinatown, Mission, South of Market, Tenderloin, Visitacion
Valley and Western Addition neighborhoods.
2. Selection Overview
The City intends to award a contract to the Proposer that meets the Minimum
Qualifications of this Solicitation whose Proposal receives the highest-ranking score.
Responsive Proposals will be evaluated by a panel (“Evaluation Panel”) consisting of
one or more parties with expertise related to goods and/or services being procured
through this Solicitation. The Evaluation Panel may include staff from various City
departments. Proposals will be evaluated based on the criteria outlined herein. If
applicable, a Contract Monitoring Division (CMD) Contract Compliance Officer will
assess Proposal compliance with Local Business Enterprise (LBE) requirements and
assign a rating bonus to Proposal scores. The CMD-adjusted scores (if applicable) will
then be tabulated, and Proposers will be ranked starting with the Proposer receiving the
highest score, then continuing with the Proposer receiving the second highest score,
and so on.
B. Anticipated Contract Term
A contract awarded pursuant to this Solicitation will begin on the day of contract
execution and end no later than June 30, 2029 with no option to renew.
C. Anticipated Contract Not to Exceed Amount
A contract awarded pursuant to this Solicitation shall have a not to exceed (“NTE”)
amount of $100,000 for the total allowable maximum term.

sections.heading: Page 3
paragraphs: D. Contract Terms and Negotiations
The successful Proposer will be required to enter into a contract substantially in the
form attached hereto as Attachment 1, City’s Contract Terms. If Proposer is unable to
accept City’s Contract Terms substantially in the form presented, Proposer shall include
a revised copy of City’s Contract Terms with its Proposal. The revised copy of City’s
Contract Terms must clearly:
(1) Mark those sections to which it objects;
(2) Set forth Proposer’s alternative terms with respect to each such section; and
(3) Explain the basis for each proposed change.
If a satisfactory contract(s) cannot be negotiated in a reasonable time, the City, in its
sole discretion, may terminate negotiations. Upon termination of negotiations, City may
begin negotiation with the Proposer that meets the Minimum Qualifications of this
Solicitation whose Proposal receives the next highest-ranking score.
E. Services Requested
This Solicitation is being issued by MOHCD. MOHCD is seeking qualified Proposers to
provide Proposals for technical assistance, policy expertise, and consulting services as
it relates to integration of housing authority functions within MOHCD’s housing work, in
accordance with Appendix A, Scope of Work.
1. Green Purchasing Requirements
In preparation for any Proposal submitted in response to this Solicitation, Proposers are
required to review the City’s Mandatory Green Purchasing Requirements to ensure all
goods and services offered to City in response to this Solicitation comply with the City’s
Green Purchasing Requirements. In addition, Proposers are encouraged to refer to
Attachment 1, City’s Contract Terms, for additional details related to the Green
Purchasing Requirements applicable to any contract awarded pursuant to this
Solicitation.

H. Minimum Qualifications Required with Proposal
Proposers must provide documentation that clearly demonstrates each Minimum

Proposal that fails to meet the Minimum Qualifications will not be eligible for further
consideration in the evaluation process . The City reserves the right to request
clarifications from Proposers prior to rejecting a Proposal for failure to meet the Minimum
Qualifications.

L. Protest Procedures
1. Protest of Contract Award
Within three (3) business days of the City's issuance of a Notice of Intent to Award, a
Proposer may submit a written Notice of Protest of Contract Award. The Notice of Protest
must include a written statement specifying in detail each and every one of the grounds
asserted for the protest. The Notice of Protest must be signed by an individual authorized
to represent the Proposer, and must cite the law, rule, local ordinance, procedure or
Solicitation provision on which the protest is based. In addition, the Notice of Protest must
specify facts and evidence sufficient for the City to determine the validity of the protest.

sections.heading: Page 6
paragraphs: 2. Delivery of Protests
A Notice of Protest must be written. Protests made orally (e.g., by telephone) will not be
considered. A Notice of Protest must be delivered by mail or email to the Contract
Administrator whose name and contact information appears on the cover page to thi s
Solicitation and received by the due dates stated above. A Notice of Protest shall be
transmitted by a means that will objectively establish the date the City received the Notice
of Protest. If a Notice of Protest is mailed, the protestor bears the risk of non- delivery
within the deadlines specified herein.

paragraphs: Appendix A
Scope of Services
1. Description of Services
MOHCD is seeking qualified suppliers to provide technical assistance, policy
expertise, and consulting services as it relates to integration of San Francisco
Housing Authority (“SFHA”) functions within MOHCD’s housing work. This
includes providing strategic advice and identification of opportunities to align
resources between and among the two agencies, interpretation of Department of
Housing and Urban Development (HUD) regulations and their applicability to
SFHA procedures and operations, process mapping, and identification of national
best practices to inform proposed program alignment.
2. Location of Work
Services will be provided at MOHCD, SFHA, at the Supplier work site, and/or
virtually.
3. Project Deliverables
The Contractor shall provide at minimum:
a. Strategic advice and potential policy around possible models of
integration, drawing on Contractor’s expertise in program structuring.
b. Identification and discussion of specific opportunities to align
resources between SFHA and MOHCD, including prioritization of
opportunities, timelines, and resource needs.
c. Review and summary of housing authority best practices that may
support SFHA in the integration effort.
d. Support for Project Based Voucher process improvement initiative
Work product and services may take the form of:
- Participation in internal and external meetings with City and SFHA staff,
contracted employees, and outside experts;
- Interviews with community partners and other stakeholders;
- Research on best practices and policy precedents
- Review and analysis of proposed policy changes and/or modifications to
current practice

sections.heading: Page 8
paragraphs: - Written memos or reports.
4. Project Schedule
Supplier should begin work immediately and work must be completed before
June 30, 2029. The supplier will meet with MOHCD and SFHA on a regular basis
to discuss progress as well as any additional topics to be investigated.
5. Reports
Contractor shall submit written reports and memos as requested by MOHCD.
The timely submission of all reports is a necessary and material term and
condition of this Agreement. If printed reports are requested, they shall be
submitted on recycled paper and printed on double-sided pages to the maximum
extent possible.
6. Department Liaison
In performing the Services provided for in this Agreement, Contractor’s liaison
with MOHCD will be Dan Adams, MOHCD Director and Lydia Ely, Deputy
Director for Housing Authority Operations.
